reason: Jo's question suggests placing the paper rider on the moving cord to see whether it travels with the wiggle.
expectation: The rider will show how the cord moves as the wiggle passes.

effect: The rider shows that the disturbance travels along the cord while the rider stays near its place. I can now explore how adjusting the cord changes its motion.
reaction: The contrast between the travelling wave and the bobbing rider is satisfying.
reason: The tension-adjusting key seems useful for changing the cord's behaviour before playing it like a string.

choice.with: Wave cord with a paper rider

expectation: Adjusting the tension will change the waves on the cord.

effect: Adjusting the tension and speed produced two stationary-looking loops, showing a repeating pattern from waves travelling in opposite directions.
reaction: The nearly still point between the moving loops is intriguing.
reason: A bridge should give the cord a defined vibrating length for playing it like a string.
expectation: The bridge will support the cord and help prepare it to be played.

effect: The bridge changes the vibrating length and passes vibration into the soundbox, preparing the cord for sound.
reaction: It is interesting that the same bridge affects both the wave pattern and sound.
reason: The soft foot pads may help support or isolate the soundbox before I play the cord.

choice.with: Cord resting on a movable bridge

expectation: The pads will fit beneath the machine and affect how its vibrations reach the bench.

choice.with: Cord resting on a movable bridge

alternatives.reason: I could try plucking the cord now, but the pads may be intended to prepare it first.

effect: The soft feet reduce vibration reaching the table, and the machine is now switched off and ready to be played.
reaction: The quieter table makes the pads' purpose clear.
reason: The plectrum is the remaining piece suited to playing the cord like a string.
expectation: Plucking the cord will make a sound through the soundbox.

effect: Plucking confirmed that the soundbox makes the cord easier to hear, and shortening its vibrating length raises the note. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The link between moving the bridge and changing the note is satisfying and easy to understand.

mostWorthwhile.text: Playing the cord and changing its vibrating length was most worthwhile: it connected the visible wave machine to an audible change in pitch.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the soft feet was the least engaging passage for me, although the quieter table made their purpose clear.

surprise.text: The rider stayed near its place while the disturbance travelled along the cord; that made the difference between the wave and the material especially clear.

arbitrary.text: The foot pads initially felt less obviously connected to the goal, but their effect on table vibration explained their purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see another construction connect a visible mechanism to an effect, as the bridge and plucked cord did here.
